I want something original rather than echoing Nighthawks directly, so I'm brainstorming night scenes—a laundromat, a drugstore corner—before landing on the idea of a lit upper-floor window as a fresher composition.

I'm settling on "Night Laundry": a street-level laundromat with a lone woman folding clothes, fluorescent light spilling onto the sidewalk in a trapezoid, a dark brick facade above with one lit window and a drawn shade. Now I'm working out the composition—landscape orientation, eye-level around a third down the frame, the building receding obliquely in Hopper's favored diagonal style.

Mapping out specific coordinates: the canvas at roughly 900x625, the night sky darkening toward a corner building on the right with a slight perspective slant to the cornice and sidewalk lines, a dark side street beyond with a distant lit window and street lamp. I'm placing a large lit shop window in the lower floor showing a simple figure at a press or counter, with three upper-floor windows, one glowing warm against the dark brick.

Thinking it through more, I decide to make this a "Cleaners" shop scene, Nighthawks-adjacent but distinct -- a woman behind the counter under fluorescent tubes, racks of garments wrapped in paper, pale yellow-green interior light spilling warmly onto the sidewalk and curb against a dark, nearly empty foreground street.

I settle on a vantage point roughly eye-level, standing across the street, with a gentle horizon line and a far vanishing point so the facade and cornice lines converge subtly rather than steeply, keeping the perspective calm and believable.

Beyond the corner of the building, I imagine the cross street opening up with darker, more distant buildings receding further away. I'm assigning value ranges to each surface: dark sky, deep brick shadows, a bright shop window as the focal highlight, warm sidewalk spill, and a dim street with a faint lit curb edge.

Now I'm thinking through the ground preparation and painting process—starting with a cream-toned lead white and ochre ground on linen, then a thin turps lay-in sketched with ultramarine lines, followed by opaque mass blocking, and finally fuller wet-over-dry layers with progressively less medium as Hopper would have worked.
